files.lesson.md: --- order: 36 unit: models9 node: AC9M9M05 n3 uses: [AC9M9M05 n2] assumes: [AC9M9M05 n2] connection: bushwalk-time title: Judge the model summary: "A model is only as good as what it assumes. Say who and what it was built for, test it against a different case, and report the answer with its limits." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The rule says 2.35 hours. A Year 9 group with full packs: more or less?" --- Naismith's rule was made for fit walkers on good tracks, carrying a light load ([bushwalk.com navigation FAQ](https://faq.bushwalk.com/FAQ_Navigation.htm), checked 25 October 2026). A Year 9 group with full packs is walking the lookout track. Should they trust the rule's 2.35 hours? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. (The group and the slower speed are made up for the task.) ## Predict: more or less ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing whether the group will be faster or slower shows whether students ask who the model was built for." check: type: predict q: "The rule gives 2.35 hours for the lookout track. A group of Year 9 students with full packs walks it. Will it take more or less than 2.35 hours?" options: - "More: they carry more and walk slower" - "Less: they are young" - "The same: the rule is exact" - "Can't say anything" actual: "More. Fit walkers on a good track carrying light loads set the rule's pace. A group with full packs is likely to be slower, so the rule would under-estimate." ``` ## Run: change the rate ```step stage: run insight: "Changing one rate in the model shows how much the answer depends on an assumption." check: { type: number, q: "Suppose the group walks at $4$ km/h on the flat. How many hours does the 8 km take? (the climb still adds 0.75)", answer: 2, explain: "8 ÷ 4 = 2 hours for the distance." } ``` ## Investigate: test the assumption ```step stage: investigate insight: "Changing the walking pace from 5 to 4 km/h shows how much a model depends on one assumption, and a report should say so." tasks: - check: type: number q: "At $4$ km/h the distance takes $2$ hours and the climb adds $0.75$ hours. What is the total? (hours)" answer: 2.75 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "2 + 0.75 = 2.75 hours." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $2 + 0.75$?", answer: 2.75, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "2 + 0.75 = 2.75." } - check: type: number q: "How many hours longer is that than the rule's $2.35$? (hours)" answer: 0.4 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "2.75 − 2.35 = 0.4 hours, about 24 minutes." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#cam" text: "Cam reports the walk's time to the teacher. Click the line where his report goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: model-outside-limits explain: "Line 3: the rule was built for fit walkers on good tracks. Cam reports it as the group's time without saying so." ``` ### Different pace ```worked \text{rule: } 8 \div 5 + 450 \div 600 = 2.35 :: Fit walkers, good track. \text{group: } 8 \div 4 + 450 \div 600 = 2.75 :: Slower pace for full packs. 2.75 - 2.35 = 0.4 :: 24 minutes longer. \text{report: about 2.4 to 2.8 hours, depending on pace} :: Give a range and the reason. ``` ### The difference ### Find the mistake Read Cam's report. Which line hides what the model assumes? ## Modify: test it elsewhere ```step stage: modify insight: "Checking the model against a different case shows where it is least reliable." tasks: - hint: ["Try both rates.", "Compare 8 ÷ 5 with 8 ÷ 4."] check: { type: number, q: "How many minutes longer is the 8 km distance at $4$ km/h than at $5$ km/h?", answer: 24, tolerance: 0.5, explain: "2 − 1.6 = 0.4 hours = 24 minutes." } - hint: ["A very steep, rough track.", "The rule only mentions distance and climb."] check: { type: question, q: "Which case is the rule LEAST likely to fit?", options: ["A rough track in hot weather with heavy packs", "A flat smooth path", "A short easy loop", "A paved road"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "A smooth path is close to what the rule was built for.", "Easy walks fit the rule.", "A paved road is the easiest case."], explain: "The rule has nothing for rough ground, heat or load, so those cases are where it can be wrong." } - hint: ["The park's own guide time is real data.", "Compare the model with it."] check: { type: question, q: "The park's sign says the lookout walk takes 3 hours up. The rule says 2.35 hours. What should you trust more for planning?", options: ["The sign, and treat the rule as a check", "The rule, because it is mathematics", "Neither", "Whichever is shorter"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "A model gives an estimate, not the truth.", "The sign comes from people who walked it.", "Shorter is risky for planning."], explain: "Real times from the track beat a rule of thumb. Use the model as a check and a way to understand." } ``` ### Minutes longer ### Where it fails ### The sign ## Practise: report the answer ```step stage: practise insight: "Giving an answer with the model's limits." tasks: - check: type: number q: "At 4 km/h on the flat, a 12 km walk with no climb takes how many hours?" answer: 3 explain: "12 ÷ 4 = 3." - check: type: question q: "Which is the best report for a trip time?" options: ["About 2.4 to 2.8 hours: the rule says 2.35 for fit walkers, and a group with packs is slower", "Exactly 2.35 hours", "Probably less", "No idea"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "No model gives an exact time.", "The reasons point to more.", "A model helps even if it's imperfect."] explain: "A good report gives a range and says what it depends on." smaller: check: { type: "question", q: "Is 'exactly 2.35 hours' a safe claim for a group with packs?", options: ["No: the rule was built for fit walkers with light loads", "Yes", "Only on flat tracks", "Only in summer"], answer: 0, explain: "The rule has no pack weight in it." } - check: type: number q: "Review: 8 km at 5 km/h plus 450 m of climb. How many hours?" answer: 2.35 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "1.6 + 0.75 = 2.35." ``` ### Another pace ### The report ### Review ## Make: report to the teacher ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the lookout: write the answer the way a planner would, with the number, the range and the reason." tasks: - hint: ["Use 4 km/h for the group.", "2 + 0.75."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The group walks at 4 km/h on the flat. Use the model with the climb at 600 m per hour: how many hours does the walk up take? (made up for the task)" steps: - ["distance: $8 \\div 4 = 2$", "hours on the flat at the group's pace"] - ["climb: $450 \\div 600 = 0.75$", "hours for the climb"] - ["$2 + 0.75 = 2.75$", "total hours"] answer: "2.75" answerLabel: "Time (hours)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["2.35", "That uses 5 km/h. Use the group's 4 km/h."] - ["2", "That's only the distance. Add the climb."] criteria: - "I used the group's pace." - "I added the climb." - "I said how it differs from the rule." explain: "2 + 0.75 = 2.75 hours, 24 minutes more than the rule's 2.35." - check: type: question q: "Which sentence is the better report?" options: ["The walk up should take about 2.75 hours for our group (the rule says 2.35 for fit walkers), so plan for about 3 hours.", "The walk takes 2.35 hours.", "The walk is long.", "The rule is wrong."] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "It hides who the rule is for.", "It gives no number.", "The rule isn't wrong, it's used outside what it was built for."] explain: "A good report gives the answer, the assumption and a margin." ``` ### The answer ### The report **Also used in** - **Planning and safety.** Every forecast and estimate needs its limits stated. - **Science.** Models are tested against real data and revised. - **Next year.** Models of change in Year 10: which model fits best. ```teacher summary: Students test a rate model against a different case and report its answer with its limits (AC9M9M05, node 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can say what a model assumes. - I can test it with different numbers. - I can report the answer with its limits. struggle: "Reporting the model's answer as fact. Ask: who was the rule made for?" before: > Students need Solve the rate model. The one idea: a model gives an estimate, and the report says what it assumes. The group pace of 4 km/h is made up for the task: real data is better (a guide time, a trial walk). running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the group's time in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student says the rule is wrong. ask: Who was it built for? fix: "It's fine for its use: it is the use for a different group that's the issue." stretch: Time a real walk and compare it with the rule. support: "A printed report frame: the answer, the range, the reason." leads: | Continues AC9M9M05 node 3. Where it leads: Year 10 modelling: which model fits. exit: q: Why report a range, not one number, from a model? a: The model is an estimate; the range shows how much depends on its assumptions. explain: | A model is only as good as what it assumes. Test it on a different case and report the answer, the range and the reason. ```

# Cam's report for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: cam
Naismith's rule: 5 km/h plus 1 hour per 600 m of climb.
The lookout walk is 8 km with 450 m of climb, so the rule gives 2.35 hours.
Report to the teacher: our walk will take 2.35 hours.
# endregion
